subject: Re: Request for fee-withholding / termination & liquidated damages alternatives to credits-only
messages:
From: Rebecca Chen <legal@mediatlas.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediAtlas Procurement <procurement@mediatlas.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request — remedies beyond credits (fee at risk / termination)

Aditya,

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Attaching a short summary of the SLA items Mediatlas requires for procurement to move forward (MediAtlas_Redwood_SLA_Summary.pdf). High-level asks: a) the ability to withhold up to 20% of monthly fees (fee-at-risk) while an outage investigation is open, b) a liquidated damages formula equal to 20% of monthly recurring charges for any month where overall uptime < 99.5%, capped at 6 months; and c) explicit termination rights for repeated SLO failures (two consecutive months under 99.5% or three months under 99.9%).

Business rationale: Mediatlas is regulated and needs stronger contractual levers than credits alone to satisfy its internal audit and executive sponsors. We are open to limited carve-outs (e.g., force majeure) but need a mechanism that materially affects vendor economics for sustained breaches.

Please confirm if Redwood can accept any of these remedies or propose a counter structure. Procurement would like the legal terms in the next pass of the MSA.

Rebecca Chen
Sr. Counsel, Mediatlas
legal@mediatlas.com
Attachment: MediAtlas_Redwood_SLA_Summary.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Chen <legal@mediatlas.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — remedies beyond credits (fee at risk / termination)

Rebecca — thanks for the note and the summary. I read through the asks and shared them with our leadership and legal. A few quick points to set expectations: Redwood’s standard commercial position is credits-only for uptime/latency SLOs, with limited capped remedies, because credits are predictable and preserve our ability to fix issues without transactional dispute. That said, we understand Mediatlas’s compliance needs and are open to discussing a narrowly scoped alternative where: 1) any fee-withholding is timeboxed and tied to an agreed investigation process, 2) any buyout/termination right has clear cure and escalation steps, and 3) liquidated damages are narrowly scoped and capped.

Can you share a little more about the audit/board trigger that drives the 6‑month cap request — is this a function of undesired economics or a procurement standard? I’m looping Marissa (sales lead) and Ben (commercial ops) to help with a pragmatic counterproposal.

Proposed next step: Aditya + Marissa + Ben + Rebecca call early next week to run through a draft.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Chen <legal@mediatlas.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — remedies beyond credits (fee at risk / termination)

Rebecca — appreciate the context. I’ve drafted a pragmatic alternative that aims to address Mediatlas’s audit ask while protecting our platform and customers. Key bullets below; I’ve attached a short draft clause for legal to review (draft-escape-clause.docx):

- Tiered immediate response: For a single calendar month where uptime < 99.5%, customer receives a 30% monthly credit for that month.
- Fee-withholding: Customer may withhold up to 15% of next month’s invoice pending completion of a formal RCA (root cause analysis) and remediation plan; withholding automatically releases or converts to credits after 45 days unless the parties jointly agree to extend.
- Liquidated damages: We cannot accept an open-ended liquidated damages calculation tied to published fees. Instead propose a limited formula: where willful negligence is proven by a third-party audit and confirmed by Redwood, liquidated damages = lesser of (3x monthly fee) or documented direct damages, with an absolute cap equal to 3 months of fees.
- Termination: Allow termination only after a sustained and uncured performance failure — defined as 3 consecutive months below 99.5% or 4 months below 99.9% — with a mandatory 30‑day cure period after written notice and a joint investigation.

This structure is meant to be a middle ground: it provides stronger economic consequences than credits-only, timeboxes withholding, and preserves a cure process so engineering can remediate before contract exit. If Mediatlas needs an escrow holdback, we could consider an OKR-based release schedule (e.g., 50% release on RCA + mitigation, 50% on post-mitigation verification).

I’m happy to join a legal-level call to walk through the wording.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft-escape-clause.docx

From: Rebecca Chen <legal@mediatlas.com>

Subject: Re: Request — remedies beyond credits (fee at risk / termination)

Marissa / Aditya — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed alternative. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal:

- The 15% withholding is a start but our internal standard is 20% for critical production dependencies; can Redwood move to 20% with the same 45-day timebox?
- The proposed liquidated damages cap at 3x monthly fees conflicts with our audit team’s ask for a 6-month economic disincentive. We would accept a lower cap if the termination trigger were faster (two consecutive months under 99.5%).
- We need assurance on immediate data export and a transition assistance clause should termination occur for performance reasons.

We are sensitive to the cure period but would like the option to terminate sooner if investigations indicate systemic failure. Attached are a few redlines from procurement (inline comments in the draft).

On the next steps: can Redwood provide a counterproposal in tracked form by Monday, 14 Sep? If so we can try to keep the timeline for our procurement committee.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Chen <legal@mediatlas.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — remedies beyond credits (fee at risk / termination) — Redwood counterproposal

Rebecca — appreciate the clear feedback and the procurement redlines. Attached is our formal counterproposal (redwood-sla-counter-proposal.pdf) but key points called out here so legal can react quickly:

1) Fee-withholding: Redwood will accept a temporary withholding of up to 20% of the next invoice while a formal RCA and remediation plan are prepared, provided: (a) withholding is limited to a 45-day period and (b) the parties agree to a mutually scoped investigation timeline. Any withheld amount automatically converts to credits if an RCA is not completed within 45 days, or releases back to Redwood if the outage is caused by customer-controlled factors.

2) Liquidated damages / cap: Redwood will not accept open-ended liquidated damages tied to ARR. We will accept a contingent damages structure where, if a third-party audit/independent verification finds willful negligence or deliberate misconduct by Redwood, damages are limited to the lesser of documented direct damages or 3x the monthly recurring charges for the impacted service, with a hard cap of 3 months of fees. This preserves an economic disincentive while protecting against speculative exposure.

3) Termination & cure: Termination for performance reasons will be allowed only after either (i) three consecutive months below 99.5% OR (ii) four months below 99.9%, and only after a 30-day written notice and joint investigation. For cases where investigation conclusively shows systemic, unremediable defects and third-party verification, either party may terminate with 30 days’ notice.

4) Transition assistance & data export: Redwood will provide 90 days of transition assistance and an expedited data export package in the event of termination for performance. We’ll carve out customer-responsible factors (e.g., misconfiguration, network issues) from any payable damages.

5) Escrow / release mechanics: Redwood will consider an escrow holdback equal to up to 1.5 months of fees with a release schedule tied to RCA milestones (50% after RCA & mitigation plan, 50% after verification). Redwood cannot agree to indefinite escrow.

Next steps: If Mediatlas accepts the structure above in principle, legal teams can work through tracked changes in the attached PDF. Otherwise, please flag the items you cannot accept and we’ll escalate internally. We’re prepared to join a call Wednesday to finalize.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood-sla-counter-proposal.pdf
